items.title: Periodic torus calculus
items.statement:
For an integer $d\ge 1$, set $\mathbb T^d:=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ and let $Q_d:=[0,2\pi]^d$ be its chosen fundamental cube. A scalar or vector field on $\mathbb T^d$ is represented by its $(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$-periodic lift to $\mathbb R^d$. For $k\ge 0$ and $m\ge 1$, $C^k_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R^m)$ consists of such lifts whose componentwise partial derivatives through order $k$ exist, are continuous and periodic, and are bounded, uniformly continuous, and Riemann integrable on $Q_d$. For a scalar field $f$ and a vector field $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_d)$, define

$$\nabla f:=(\partial_1 f,\ldots,\partial_d f),\qquad \operatorname{div}v:=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jv_j,\qquad \Delta f:=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_j^2f.$$

The integral of an integrable scalar field over $\mathbb T^d$ means its Riemann integral over $Q_d$. For a matrix field $A=(A_{ij})$, $|A|^2:=\sum_{i,j}|A_{ij}|^2$. The notation $C^1([0,T];C^k_{\rm per})$ means that the field is continuously differentiable in time in the supremum norms of its spatial derivatives through order $k$. These are dimensionless mathematical conventions; they assign no physical units.

references.title: Stefanos Georgiadis, Energy identity for the incompressible Cahn–Hilliard/Navier–Stokes system with non-degenerate mobility
references.locator: §1, p. 1: the source fixes the periodic convention T^3=(R/2πZ)^3; the definition here gives its coordinatewise d-dimensional version.

items.title: Periodic integration by parts on a flat torus
items.statement:
Let $d\ge 1$, let $g\in C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R)$, and let $F\in C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R^d)$. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb T^d}\operatorname{div}F\,dx=0,\qquad \int_{\mathbb T^d}\nabla g\cdot F\,dx=-\int_{\mathbb T^d}g\,\operatorname{div}F\,dx.$$

references.title: Stefanos Georgiadis, Energy identity for the incompressible Cahn–Hilliard/Navier–Stokes system with non-degenerate mobility
references.locator: §2, pp. 3–7: periodic mollification and integration-by-parts identities in the T^3 argument; the d-dimensional coordinate proof below is local.

items.title: Periodic Cahn–Hilliard incompressible flow system
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, a time interval $[0,T]$ with $T>0$, constants $\varepsilon,M,\nu>0$, and a potential $W\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ that is bounded below. Use the torus, integral, periodic-lift, and time-regularity conventions of periodic torus calculus, with all spatial derivatives taken on the lifts. For vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^d$, write $a\cdot b=\sum_{j=1}^d a_jb_j$ and $|a|^2=a\cdot a$; set $(\Delta u)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_j^2u_i$, $(\nabla u)_{ij}=\partial_j u_i$, and $(u\cdot\nabla)f=\sum_{j=1}^du_j\partial_jf$, componentwise when $f$ is vector-valued. Write $\nabla\cdot u=\operatorname{div}u$. A classical tuple consists of periodic fields $u:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R^d$, $\phi:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$, and $\pi:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$, with $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2_{\rm per})$, $\phi\in C^1([0,T];C^1_{\rm per})\cap C([0,T];C^2_{\rm per})$, and $\pi\in C([0,T];C^1_{\rm per})$. Define the chemical-potential field, which is not an independent unknown, by

$$\mu_c:=\varepsilon^{-1}W'(\phi)-\varepsilon\Delta\phi,$$

and require $\mu_c\in C([0,T];C^2_{\rm per})$ so that its Laplacian is pointwise defined. The dimensionless periodic incompressible phase-flow system is

$$\partial_t\phi+u\cdot\nabla\phi=M\Delta\mu_c,\qquad \partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u-\phi\nabla\mu_c,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0.$$

Here $\phi$ is a scalar order parameter; “diffuse interface” refers only to representing interfacial structure through this field and its spatial-gradient energy. The scalar $\pi$ is the multiplier enforcing the divergence constraint. The associated total energy is

$$E(t):=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\left(\frac12|u(t,x)|^2+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}|\nabla\phi(t,x)|^2+\varepsilon^{-1}W(\phi(t,x))\right)\,dx.$$

All coefficients and fields in this definition are dimensionless mathematical quantities; no physical units, empirical calibration, sharp-interface limit, or claim that $\phi$ is a probability or positive density is asserted. A physical identification requires additional density, phase-scale, surface-energy, length/time-scale, and chemical-potential units.

references.title: J. Tinsley Oden, Lecture Notes, Fall 2016, Chapter 11: Phase-Field Models
Stefanos Georgiadis, Energy identity for the incompressible Cahn–Hilliard/Navier–Stokes system with non-degenerate mobility
references.locator: §1, p. 1, equations (1.1)–(1.5), for the periodic coupled-system convention and source formulation.

items.title: Cancellation of capillary and transport energy exchange
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, $\varepsilon,M,\nu>0$, and $W\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be bounded below. On $\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$, let $u:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R^d$, $\phi:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$, and $\pi:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be periodic fields with

$$u\in C^1([0,T];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R^d)),\qquad \phi\in C^1([0,T];C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R))\cap C([0,T];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R)),\qquad \pi\in C([0,T];C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R)).$$

Define $\mu_c:=\varepsilon^{-1}W'(\phi)-\varepsilon\Delta\phi$ and assume that this defined field belongs to $C([0,T];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R))$, so its gradient and Laplacian in the equations below are pointwise defined. Suppose the fields satisfy pointwise

$$\partial_t\phi+u\cdot\nabla\phi=M\Delta\mu_c,\qquad \partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u-\phi\nabla\mu_c,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0.$$

For the energy

$$E(t):=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\left(\frac12|u(t,x)|^2+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}|\nabla\phi(t,x)|^2+\varepsilon^{-1}W(\phi(t,x))\right)\,dx,$$

where $|\nabla u|^2=\sum_{i,j=1}^d|\partial_j u_i|^2$, the exact conditional identity is

$$\frac{dE}{dt}(t)=-\nu\int_{\mathbb T^d}|\nabla u(t,x)|^2\,dx-M\int_{\mathbb T^d}|\nabla\mu_c(t,x)|^2\,dx\qquad(0<t<T).$$

references.title: J. Tinsley Oden, Lecture Notes, Fall 2016, Chapter 11: Phase-Field Models
Stefanos Georgiadis, Energy identity for the incompressible Cahn–Hilliard/Navier–Stokes system with non-degenerate mobility
references.locator: §1, equations (1.1)–(1.10), and §2, Theorem 1 proof, pp. 1–7; the source's weak-solution assumptions are not used here.

items.title: Constant phase is an energy-stationary state
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, $\varepsilon,M,
u>0$, $W\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be bounded below, and $c\in\mathbb R$. On $\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$, consider the periodic equations $\partial_t\phi+u\cdot
abla\phi=M\Delta\mu_c$, $\partial_tu+(u\cdot
abla)u+
abla\pi=
u\Delta u-\phi
abla\mu_c$, and $
abla\cdot u=0$, with $\mu_c=\varepsilon^{-1}W'(\phi)-\varepsilon\Delta\phi$. The constant fields $u=0$, $\phi=c$, and $\pi=0$ solve this system with constant chemical potential $\mu_c=\varepsilon^{-1}W'(c)$. Their total energy is $E(t)=(2\pi)^d\varepsilon^{-1}W(c)$ for all $t\in[0,T]$, so this is an energy-stationary state, meaning that its energy is constant in time; no local-minimum or stability claim is made. All quantities are dimensionless mathematical variables.
